what: official DeepSeek TileKernels Engram gate kernels adapted with a 128-element tile / 1-warp-per-head backward so the nano dims 384/640 run natively without padding; vendored under nanov41/engram_kernels (MIT).
changes_vs_upstream: fwd: blk_d candidates add 128; vec_size = 8 if blk_d>=256 else 4 (threads=32)
bwd: warps_per_head = 2 if hidden_size%256==0 else 1 (128 threads); v_copy_vec_size chosen dynamically for the nano hidden sizes; single-warp dldg reduction instead of the hardcoded two-warp sum

d12_tuned_graph_step_ms.shape: b=16 x seq=1024, graph-only, 2 rounds, final_env + R69 flags
d12_tuned_graph_step_ms.conclusion: nano TileLang is statistically tied with the Inductor-fused gate (+4.5% vs +3.9%) and ~8% faster than the padded official path (73.2 ms); it is now the default fused path, Inductor remains available via NANOV41_ENGRAM_TL=0 NANOV41_ENGRAM_COMPILE=1.

d20_full_graph.note: CE head v3 falls back to bf16 for dim 640; d20 path is validated for capture/kernel correctness, not compared for MFU.
